title: SICK - Secure and Govern Growth and Data Science Team Meeting
decisions: Allen has been appointed as acting full-stack manager for security policies.
Anti-abuse is being moved into the data science section, with data science becoming the renamed section covering the existing model ops and anti-abuse groups.
A second team will be established within dynamic analysis without creating a new group, with the split based on feature categories.
The development team will close the MR-rate improvement issue and link the meeting notes.
The team will continue using the existing Google Docs for talent assessments until Workday access and the exact process are available.
The team will use the engineering project/team member handbook entries as the source for maintainer information rather than relying solely on reviewer roulette.

actionItems.task: Compile and report on team allocations, error budgets, reliability, and security incidents.
Continue working through the handbook and organizational changes associated with moving anti-abuse into data science.
Set up and maintain the container security bot that weekly asks the team for volunteers to resource the required data.
Report back on interview refinement changes.
Continue experimenting with refinement meetings and smaller work items to improve engineering velocity and MR rate.
Brainstorm and discuss options for handling security findings related to commercial analyzer versions, including deviation requests and bulk fixes.
Run the proposed 'Enrichment' team name past David de Santo and determine whether organizational approval is required.
Add announcements for work anniversaries and new hires to the meeting template.
Provide feedback on the development vision, mission, and direction.
Add maintainers to individual team-member YAML files in the handbook for projects that require them.

risks: Security issues associated with dependency and container scanning may require remediation plans for FedRAMP-compliant or certified feature categories, including cases involving false positives or projects that do not provide fixes.
Changes to team structure, approvals, security processes, and maintainer requirements may create additional coordination overhead or delays.
